+When the column is given by name (``loc``) and the row by position (``iloc``),
+you either need to convert the column name to its position using
+:meth:`Index.get_loc` or you need to convert the row position to its index.
+Both variants are shown in the following example.
+The ``iloc`` variant works as a direct replacement of the chained assignment
+``df["foo"].iloc[0] = 100`` while the ``loc`` variant first translates the
+position to the index and then finds all positions with that index. It does
+more work and is only equivalent if the DataFrame has a unique row index.
+Note that many such statements in the code can potentially hurt performance.
+If possible, prefer to update the whole column at once. If you have a boolean
